strings.name: Sebastian Siemiatkowski
strings.summary: Siemiatkowski co-founded Klarna while studying in Stockholm, linking merchant checkout, deferred payments and consumer credit, later building European banking operations and entering the US. The company experienced a sharp valuation reset and AI-service changes before its 2025 New York listing; he remains CEO.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: He co-founded Klarna and advanced online payments and consumer credit, influencing European fintech and digital retail.
strings.facts.f1.label: Main business
strings.facts.f1.value: Merchant checkout, deferred payments, installment credit and retail banking.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Master’s in Economics and Business, Stockholm School of Economics, 2007.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Connecting payments and credit in shopping
strings.highlights.h1.text: With fellow founders and teams, he linked merchant collections with consumer payment arrangements, expanding into a cross-market network and banking.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Adjusting through growth and pressure
strings.highlights.h2.text: Funding valuations and AI-service disputes prompted changes in cost and service strategy; listing did not remove lending, regulatory and operational responsibilities.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Applying for a US bank license
strings.timeline.t1.text: Klarna submitted applications to Utah regulators and the FDIC for an industrial bank; an application was not approval or the start of that bank’s operations.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Klarna lists in New York
strings.timeline.t2.text: Shares began trading as KLAR; he also acknowledged excessive emphasis on AI cost-cutting and shifted focus toward products and service.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Reporting AI assistant performance
strings.timeline.t3.text: The company said its first month handled about two-thirds of service chats, equivalent to 700 full-time agents’ workload; this was an estimate, not a count of layoffs at launch.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Raising funds at a lower valuation
strings.timeline.t4.text: Klarna raised $800 million at a $6.7 billion post-money valuation, well below 2021’s $45.6 billion, reflecting financial-market and business pressures.
strings.timeline.t5.title: European banking authorization
strings.timeline.t5.text: Klarna became a licensed bank operating in the European Economic Area, extending its payments business into more financial products.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Entering the US market
strings.timeline.t6.text: Partnerships including Macy’s brought its buy-now-pay-later offering to US consumers and supported international expansion.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Acquiring Sofort
strings.timeline.t7.text: Klarna bought the German online-payments company, extending account-payment technology and its European network.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completing his master’s
strings.timeline.t8.text: After founding the business, he completed Economics and Business studies at the Stockholm School of Economics.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Co-founding Klarna
strings.timeline.t9.text: With Niklas Adalberth and Victor Jacobsson in Stockholm, he established a payments company and became CEO, pursuing simpler online shopping payments.
